newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour - jobs "bottom line" for EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour - jobs "bottom line" for EMU entry.

text.p: Robin Cook, the opposition Labour Party's foreign affairs spokesman, said on Tuesday the European single market would work better with a single currency.
But he said European governments had to set objectives for tackling unemployment.
"Jobs will be the bottom line by which we judge whether Britain will join any single currency," Cook told the Labour Party's annual conference in Blackpool.

"The single market would work better with a single currency. But Britain will only benefit if we can compete on level terms," Cook told the conference, the last before a general election due in the next seven months.
"That is why Labour believes that for Britain to join a single currency we need first to achieve convergence of economic performance in the real world of output, of investment and of jobs."
Cook said a Labour government would also end the British opt-out to the Social Chapter and sign up for it by the end of 1997, before it took over the EU presidency.
Cook said Labour was keen to press ahead with enlarging the European Union to take in the countries of central and Eastern Europe.
Negotiations for their application would begin during a British presidency which starts in January 1998, he said.
Cook said Labour had therefore appointed a special envoy from the party to the countries who had applied for EU membership.
He said British ambassador to the EU, Sir Michael Butler, had accepted the role of special envoy.
